Definition: from G1537 and teino (to stretch); to extend:--cast, put forth, stretch forth (out).
BiblicalUsage: ekteínō is how Scripture says to stretch forth. In Matthew 8:3, the text says "And Jesus put forth [his] hand." In Mark 1:41, the text says "put forth [his] hand."
TheologicalSignificance: I take ekteínō to mean that healing is God's work, in His time and His way, and He is able. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: Jesus Heals a Man with Leprosy; Jesus Appears to Seven Disciples by the Sea of Galilee
